subject: Accept flow created duplicate profile — W-9 stuck, PO provisioning on hold
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@asteriumlogistics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T08:20:00-04:00
Subject: Issue after accepting Redwood invite — W-9 attaching to old account

Hi Jordan,

We accepted the supplier portal invite this morning but ran into two problems:

- After clicking Accept, the portal mentions “Account exists — choose profile” and shows an older Asterium profile we created years ago.
- The W-9 we just uploaded appears attached to that old profile (see attachment) and the new account shows no tax docs.

Because of this mismatch, the PO (Ref 45923) is still stuck in provisioning and our AP team can't receive invoices. I attached the W-9 we uploaded and a screenshot of the accept error.

Can you advise next steps? We need POs released this week to meet our vendor cutoff.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Vendor Onboarding
Asterium Logistics
Attachments: w9-signed.pdf (application/pdf); accept-error.png (image/png)

- Vendor: Asterium Logistics (Olivia Park)

- Attachments: w9-signed.pdf, accept-error.png (from vendor)

- Ben: can you check whether the accept flow created a duplicate profile (likely via subaddressing) and whether we can merge the two identities and rebind the W-9 to the active account?
- Monica: please place PO 45923 on manual hold/notes so it doesn't auto-cancel and let Finance know we're remediating.

Vendor is pushing for a same-week resolution. I have asked them to hold for our next update. See vendor note below.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T11:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Issue after accepting Redwood invite — W-9 attaching to old account

Thanks for the heads up.

Triage notes:
- Initial look: logs show two profiles tied to the same normalized email but different external IDs (legacy import + new invite flow). The accept flow defaulted to the legacy profile because the vendor previously created a light-weight account.
- Because tax docs are attached at profile-level, uploads went to the legacy record and didn't cascade.

Immediate fix options:
1) Manual merge: reassign the legacy profile's documents to the new active account and rebind payment methods. Time: ~2 business hours. Risk: low but requires audit log entry.
2) Vendor re-upload to a one-time upload URL tied to the active account (low friction). I'll generate this and send to Olivia.

Next steps I will take now:
- Create merge ticket and schedule manual merge (tracking RT-78342).
- Generate one-time upload link and send it to Olivia with DocuSign ask as fallback.

Olivia — please re-upload the W-9 here when you receive the link. If you prefer DocuSign, use the template link below and we'll pull the signed doc into the active profile.

DocuSign (fallback): https://docusign.com/templates/tn-0134
ETA for merge: ~2 hours; I'll update once complete.

Ben
Senior Ops Engineer
Attachments referenced: manual-merge-checklist.txt (text)

Hi Olivia — quick update and plan:

We found a legacy/light profile linked to your email that the accept flow associated with; this caused your W-9 to attach to the older record. Ben is performing a manual merge and has created a ticket (RT-78342). Expected timeline is ~2 hours from now.

Action for you (choose one):
- Option A (recommended): Use this one-time upload link that I will send in a separate email — upload that W-9 there and we'll bind it to your active profile immediately.
- Option B: Sign/upload via DocuSign using this template: https://docusign.com/templates/tn-0134

PO 45923 will be held during remediation; Finance has been notified.

I'll follow up when the merge completes and the PO is released.

Thanks for the quick response and apologies for the friction.
